episode_thesis: Trend following has recovered after a hard H1 2025 (a three-day Liberation Day magnitude shock that fell outside any backtest), led by equities and precious metals, with fixed income and short-term traders the laggards. Kaminski's core method claim is that strategies should be judged on out-of-sample results and robustness to parameter choices, then combined across schools, price trend with economic trend, and viewed as part of a total portfolio. Both speakers argue trend is a true diversifier whose value is greatest in stress and unstable inflation, and expect more private-wealth money to alternatives.

speakers.name: Katie Kaminski
speakers.role: Co-host; trend-following researcher and portfolio manager (Boston)
speakers.speaker_note: Caption spells 'Katie Kaminsky'. Ledger corrections moved the inflation study and Dunn track-record remarks (C03-3, C03-4) to the host; they are not hers.

worldview_premises.premise: A total-portfolio view values trend following more than a bucket-by-bucket view, because trend is one of the few strategies whose effect is risk reduction for the whole portfolio, which line-item optimisation hides.
worldview_premises.support: Locally optimal versus globally optimal; success of risk-mitigation buckets; no data offered in this episode.

worldview_premises.premise: It is easy to overfit the past, so a strategy is only credible if its statistics stay stable when the parameter choices are permuted and if it holds out of sample.
worldview_premises.support: Reasoning from the problem of living forward in time; no study cited.

worldview_premises.premise: No single parameter school (fixed or dynamic, recent or long data, per-market or common) is reliable, because each banks on one view of the world; aggregating several is the most diversified choice.
worldview_premises.support: Philosophical argument; the example is that bonds under a divided Fed may not behave as in the past.

worldview_premises.premise: Trend following is most valuable in stress: in the worst equity quintiles it shows convexity, because in stress fundamentals matter less than price changes. In calm positive-fundamental years such as 2025 it matters less and economic trend can win.
worldview_premises.support: Her plot of SG Trend returns by equity-return quintile, presented in an academic talk that week.

worldview_premises.premise: Large turbulent (high magnitude surprise) days hurt CTAs and normally recover within a day or so; a sustained three-day shock is outside the backtest and is hard for trend systems.
worldview_premises.support: Her own turbulence-metrics paper; Liberation Day is the first three-day case in her data.

worldview_premises.premise: Macro managers and trend followers mostly harvest the same global trends across asset classes by different entry methods, so macro returns correlate highly with trend.
worldview_premises.support: A coming paper on macro trading, not yet public.

worldview_premises.premise: Managed futures lift outcomes for individuals, who live one sample path, because they cut maximum drawdown in equity-heavy portfolios and so reduce the chance of retiring into a crash.
worldview_premises.support: Cash-flow model of target-retirement portfolios (unfinished); 2008 example.

worldview_premises.premise: Some managed futures added to stocks and bonds improves diversification more than expected because it is one of few really different return sources.
worldview_premises.support: Alternatives-completion work at her firm; no numbers given.

mechanism_chains.topic: Why trend struggled in H1 2025 and recovered in H2

steps.why: Markets had to assess a shock before the macro world had actually changed.

steps.from: three consecutive days of magnitude surprise
steps.why: A one-day shock is bounded, a three-day consistent move is large and sits outside the backtest; the trend follower must balance trend strength against volatility.

steps.from: headline risk calms and macro change shows up
steps.to: more consistent price trends in Q3-Q4
steps.why: With less noise, trends persist and trend systems get paid.

mechanism_chains.evidence: Quarterly pattern of trend returns; her turbulence data series ('lots of years') in which the three-day run is unique.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: She says one-off events lack statistical significance, so the mechanism cannot be confirmed and she would not change the model mechanically.

mechanism_chains.topic: Why economic trend helped in 2025 and when it will not

steps.from: headline risk causes chaos in price trends
economic trend follows overall themes of the economy
steps.why: Fundamentals stayed positive (S&P +16%), so a macro-theme signal ignored the price swings.
Prices change faster than data; trend's convexity appears in the worst equity quintiles.

mechanism_chains.evidence: AQR's 2025 result as reported in a CityWire article (relayed by the host), and her quintile plot.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Macro indicators can also predict a trend that never occurs; economic trend is 'more art', essentially macro under another name; official data can go missing (40-day US gap).

mechanism_chains.topic: Why unstable inflation helps trend followers

steps.from: inflation surges in one pocket (electricity) and falls in others

steps.why: Inflation is itself about how much prices move.

mechanism_chains.evidence: Only the host's track-record observation (C03-4); her own remark is a theoretical link.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Not stated; she notes bonds were hard for trend even in 18 months of fairly stable inflation (host).

decision_process.practice: Rank strategies first on out-of-sample results and on how stable the performance statistics stay when the (about five) parameters are permuted; then check downside capture, upside capture and Sharpe.
decision_process.why: It is easy to overfit the past; the decisions you made must not drive the statistics.

decision_process.practice: Combine parameter schools: fixed and dynamic parameters, recent and long data, per-market and common settings; machine-learning adaptation can add some value over a classic moving-average crossover.
decision_process.why: Any single school banks too much on one view; the past may not resemble the present.

decision_process.practice: Do not change the model after a one-off shock such as Liberation Day, but re-examine how volatility estimation and signals respond to sustained shocks.
decision_process.why: Three days is not statistically significant, yet it was not in the backtest.

decision_process.practice: Combine price trend with economic/macro strategies depending on the investor's mandate; risk-mitigation clients keep trend for its stress behaviour and accept modest results in strong equity years.
decision_process.why: Each approach has days of sunshine and rain.

decision_process.practice: Reach private-wealth and model-portfolio channels through wrappers like ETFs and by educating model-portfolio researchers.
decision_process.why: Private wealth is the next wave of allocations to alternatives.

speakers.evidence_style: Mixed: her own published research (turbulence metrics, crisis-alpha quintile plots, target-retirement cash-flow model), first-principles reasoning on robustness and diversification; little hard data stated in the episode itself.

current_views.view: Trend following is working again: H1 2025 was hard after Liberation Day, H2 much better as calmer markets show consistent trends.
current_views.reasoning: Headline noise faded and macro change began to show in prices.

current_views.view: Precious metals surged as a hedge alongside equities with a weak dollar, possibly aided by central bank buying.
current_views.reasoning: Investors hold equities but buy the safe asset as insurance.

current_views.view: Fixed income trends were hard because the market wants US cuts that are not delivered, though risk in the asset class may now be lower and interesting next year; energies went back and forth.
current_views.reasoning: Waiting for cuts that do not arrive.

current_views.view: The weak-dollar theme shows a pivot, unclear whether it reflects an expected slowdown and unexpected cuts or a bottom after a large move.
Inflation can re-emerge in pockets (electricity, US healthcare, insurance); price rises arrive unevenly but drift up, so inflation matters for the next few years.
current_views.reasoning: Uneven price rises in specific sectors.

current_views.view: A very long-term view that ignored early-year noise helped in 2025; faster systems traded whipsaws.
A wave of private wealth money into alternatives is coming.
current_views.reasoning: Concern about 60/40 and new access products.

speakers.name: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
speakers.role: Host (Top Traders Unplugged); hedge fund manager
speakers.speaker_note: Caption spells 'Neils Kostrup Larsen'. Ledger corrections assign to him the inflation study and the Dunn track-record points, and the price-is-truth point.

worldview_premises.premise: Price data is the pure, hard-to-manipulate signal, while official economic data can be delayed, manipulated or missing; the market price is the only truth.
worldview_premises.support: Industry saying; the 40-day US data gap and the firing of the data head as illustration.

worldview_premises.premise: Trend following does well in high and rising inflation, and what matters is the instability of inflation, not its level.
worldview_premises.support: A long inflation study at his firm and Dunn's track record: worst CTA era 2000-2019 (low, stable inflation); fastest compounding 1982-2000 (low but unstable inflation).

worldview_premises.premise: Pure trend following does not predict and cannot anticipate, because it needs price data and time to adjust; every approach, including systematic macro, has sunshine and lean periods.
worldview_premises.support: IPM (Swedish systematic macro) example: strong record, then stopped working and closed.

worldview_premises.premise: Fiduciaries who give trend zero or 1% are hard to justify because no paper shows trend fails to add value to a portfolio.
worldview_premises.support: Twenty years of thinking about fiduciary duty; absence of contrary white papers.

worldview_premises.premise: Private equity and private credit are familiar equity and credit exposure in another wrapper, so only trend-like strategies are real alternatives.
worldview_premises.support: Assertion; the Dunn crisis-period paper he mentions is the supporting reference.

worldview_premises.premise: Funds that judge each holding by what it adds to the whole portfolio (total portfolio approach; Hawaii pension dropped buckets) should move trend following up their list of valuable components.
worldview_premises.support: Hawaii pension anecdote (former head, now at Goldman Sachs); Calpers vote on total portfolio approach cited as context; no data.

worldview_premises.premise: Equity trends are supported by heavy fund inflows until politicians disrupt them.
worldview_premises.support: A Deutsche Bank chart of weekly equity fund flows against the 2010-2024 median.

mechanism_chains.topic: AI data centres to electricity prices to inflation

steps.from: AI build-out (data-centre spending up about 400% in two years)
steps.why: US data centres use 183 TWh, expected to more than double in 4-5 years; 26% of Virginia supply.

steps.to: electricity prices as a new inflation source
steps.why: He offers it as a good guess for where inflation could come from; no price evidence.

mechanism_chains.evidence: Ed Yardeni blog post, relayed second-hand.

mechanism_chains.topic: Unstable inflation as the regime for trend

steps.to: best compounding in Dunn's trend record
steps.why: Contrast with the stable-inflation 2000-2019 worst period.

steps.from: central banks unable to control inflation
steps.why: Not constant 8-10% inflation but uncontrollable inflation.

mechanism_chains.evidence: One firm's track record over two periods; no other CTAs or statistics.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Not stated; he notes bonds were hard for trend followers even with stable inflation over 18 months.

decision_process.practice: Treat price as the primary truth; consider per-market trend parameters informed by market elasticity (reaction speed), without overoptimising.
decision_process.why: Some markets react faster than others.

decision_process.practice: Know the end client; ETF flows hide the investor's identity, so a manager cannot stop clients from reallocating at the wrong time (such as after Q2 2025).
decision_process.why: Reaching clients avoids unnecessary hardship from badly timed allocations.

speakers.evidence_style: Relays articles, data series and index prints (Deutsche Bank, Yardeni, CityWire on AQR, Capgemini, SG indices) and his firm's track record; anecdotes (IPM). Hosting role, so few self-built tests.

current_views.view: Markets barely reacted to 40 days without official US data, so routine data is perhaps not essential.
Expect an unstable, uncontrollable inflation environment resembling 1982-2000, which favours trend.
October 2025 started soft but trend followers re-aligned with longer trends: equities and precious metals strong, softs mixed, currencies recovering, fixed income the main challenge.

Metals-led commodity gains (silver +73%, platinum +68%, gold +59% YTD) show why commodities belong in trend portfolios; trend indices were around flat to +2.6% YTD, BTOP50 up five of the last six years.
Short-term traders lagged in 2025 (-4.8% vol-adjusted) despite many short-term corrections.
current_views.reasoning: Event-risk whipsaws; frequency mismatch (view shared by Kaminski).

current_views.view: AQR coped well in 2025 by mixing price trend with economic trend (50/50 in one program) and single-name equities, while headline risk caused chaos in price trends.
current_views.reasoning: Relayed from a CityWire article; he flags that the no-data period will test it.

current_views.view: Alternatives could grow from about $4 trillion to $12 trillion by 2034 (Everest Group: $30 trillion by 2030), with private wealth and family offices allocating far more than institutions.
current_views.reasoning: Capgemini and Everest Group projections as cited.

current_views.view: Bank QIS and similar systematic strategies exceed official CTA assets yet are opaque, so disclosure regulation is suggested.

disagreements.topic: Can economic trend anticipate, or is it still reactive?

positions.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
positions.position: Pure trend following does not predict or anticipate; economic trend sounds a little predictive, and all approaches, like IPM, have lean periods.

positions.speaker: Katie Kaminski
positions.position: Economic trend is a way to take the same global trends by a different entry method; it filtered noise in 2025 but is an art and can predict trends that never occur.

positions.speaker: Katie Kaminski
positions.position: In stress, price trend wins as fundamentals become irrelevant; in calm positive-fundamental years economic trend can win; the mix depends on mandate.

positions.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
positions.position: Recent economic-trend performance is the 'sunshine' phase; he warns the pattern may reverse like IPM's.

gaps_and_conflicts.issue: The mechanism for why unstable inflation helps trend is theoretical; the only evidence is one firm's track record over two eras, offered by the host, and C03-4 is not statistically tested.
Kaminski's evidence on turbulence (three-day Liberation Day run) is a single event with no significance, as she admits.
Several quantitative figures (alternatives to $12tn, Everest $30tn, 183 TWh, 400% data-centre spend) are second-hand and the caption mangles 'sensors' for the facilities that house chips.
Target-retirement and macro-vs-trend papers are unfinished, so conclusions about worst-case improvement are asserted not shown.
Host cites BTOP50 'up four of five years including this year' then corrects to 'five of the last six'; only 2023 (-1.85%) was down.

forward_looking_inputs: (reader) Inputs named as leading or conditioning future trend returns: inflation instability across pockets (electricity, healthcare, insurance) rather than the level; whether central banks deliver the US cuts markets expect (fixed income trends); dollar direction (slowdown and cuts versus bottoming); equity fund flows as support for the equity trend; sustained multi-day magnitude surprises as a regime in which trend systems struggle; restoration of official data for economic-trend signals. Horizons are the next few years for inflation, and roughly a year for fixed income ('next year perhaps').
reader_inferences: (reader) Kaminski's robustness test implies a parameter-permutation sensitivity metric could be a candidate screen for any strategy in a backtest framework.

(reader) Both speakers frame trend as a crisis hedge in stress and an inflation-instability play, yet they also say trend was only modest in the strong-equity regime of 2025; value is regime-dependent rather than constant.
(reader) The unstable-inflation thesis rests on one track record (Dunn) and may be confounded by the 1980s-90s interest-rate regime.
